meta.title: Building and Testing a Least-Privilege IAM Role

slides.title: Building and Testing a Least-Privilege IAM Role
What Gets Built
slides.lead: This practical builds one IAM role that can view and start EC2 instances but cannot terminate them, then proves that scope using the IAM Policy Simulator rather than a live EC2 action
slides.notes: Practical overview: walk the six steps in order before opening the console. The role is proved with the IAM Policy Simulator, not with a live EC2 action.

slides.title: Reading Permissions
slides.lead: Before writing a policy, it helps to read one AWS already ships, to see which services, access levels and resources it allows

step.text: AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess managed policy details page, Permissions tab active

slides.notes: Practical step 1: open the AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess managed policy and read its Permissions tab.

slides.title: Describe-Only JSON
slides.lead: The custom policy starts narrow: it allows only the EC2 describe action, nothing else, so the role begins with the smallest workable grant

step.text: IAM policy editor in JSON mode, one statement allowing `ec2:DescribeInstances`

slides.notes: Practical step 2: the policy editor in JSON mode with one statement allowing ec2:DescribeInstances.

slides.title: Attached Permissions
slides.lead: After the role is created and the custom policy attached, the role's own Permissions tab confirms exactly one policy is attached before any testing begins

step.text: IAM role Permissions tab listing one attached customer-managed policy

slides.notes: Practical step 3: the role's Permissions tab lists one attached customer-managed policy.

slides.title: Closing The Gap
slides.lead: Once the simulator shows the start action denied, the policy is edited to add exactly that permission, and nothing else, before testing again
slides.notes: Practical steps 4 to 6: record the simulator results, add exactly the missing permission, retest, then discuss the over-permissive policy and the trust relationship.

slides.title: Scope Confirmed
slides.lead: The finished role lets its holder view and start EC2 instances but never terminate them, with every permission traceable to one explicit statement in its policy
